The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

<output>
Arguments passed on the command line will always override those
specified in configuration files. An example configuration file
is available at
[tex-fmt.toml](https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/blob/main/tex-fmt.toml).
To ignore all config files, use the `--noconfig` flag.

Note for contributors: this repository's configuration file will be
automatically applied if tex-fmt is run from within the repository.
Use `--noconfig` or `--config <PATH>` to avoid this.

### Disabling the formatter

Ending a source line with `% tex-fmt: skip` disables formatting for that line.
To disable the formatter for a block, use `% tex-fmt: off` and `% tex-fmt: on`.

``` tex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

    This line is skipped % tex-fmt: skip

% tex-fmt: off
  These lines are also
    not formatted or wrapped
% tex-fmt: on

\end{document}
```

Verbatim environments including `verbatim`, `Verbatim`, `lstlisting`
and `minted` are automatically skipped.

### Ignoring files in recursive mode

Recursive searches with `--recursive` or `-r` will
ignore patterns in `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files,
following git conventions.

### Shell completion

Shell completion scripts can be generated at run-time using the
`--completion <SHELL>` flag. See the
[completion](
https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/tree/main/completion)
directory for more details.

### Man page

A man page can be generated at run-time using the
`--man` flag. See the
[man](https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/tree/main/man)
directory for more details.

### Pre-commit hook

tex-fmt can be run before every git commit using
[pre-commit](http://pre-commit.com) with the following
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` in your repository root:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt
    rev: v0.5.6
    hooks:
      - id: tex-fmt
```

To prevent the pre-commit hook from modifying your files, add:

```yaml
      - id: tex-fmt
        args: [--check]
```

## Performance

When formatting all of the test cases,
tex-fmt is over a thousand times faster than latexindent.

| **Files** | **Lines** | **Size** | **tex-fmt** | **latexindent** | **latexindent -m** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 51 | 94k | 3.5M | **0.055s** | 106s [x1927] | 127s [x2309] |

## Contribution

Please feel free to open an issue or submit a pull request,
including as much information as you can. Documentation of internals
can be accessed by cloning this repository and running `cargo doc`,
or by visiting the [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tex-fmt/latest/tex_fmt/) page.

Alternatively, you can
[Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/wgunderwood)!

## Limitations

- Semantic parsing of LaTeX code not conducted
- No linting or correction of syntax errors
- Compliance with existing formatting guidelines not guaranteed
- No spelling or grammar checking

## Existing tools

- [latexindent](https://github.com/cmhughes/latexindent.pl).
Perl script, many configuration options, slow on large files

- [bibtex-tidy](https://github.com/FlamingTempura/bibtex-tidy).
JavaScript program, specifically for BibTeX files

- [LaTeXTidy](http://bfc.sfsu.edu/cgi-bin/hsu.pl?LaTeX_Tidy).
Perl script, download links seem to be broken

- [latex-pretty](https://c.albert-thompson.com/latex-pretty/).
Browser-based, uses latexindent as the backend

- [latexformat.com](https://latexformat.com/).
Browser-based

- [texpretty](http://ftp.math.utah.edu/pub/texpretty/).
C program which works sometimes and appears to be fast

- [latex-editor](https://latex-editor.pages.dev/formatter/).
Browser-based

- [LaTeXFmt](https://github.com/engeljh/vim-latexfmt).
Vim plugin, does not apply indentation

- [latex-formatter](https://github.com/nfode/latex-formatter).
Visual Studio plugin, uses latexindent as the backend

- [LLF](https://repo.or.cz/llf.git).
Lua script, many configuration options

## Options

### Command line options

The following arguments can be passed on the command line.

| Option                 | Alias | Default | Description |
| ---------------------- | ----- | ------- | --- |
| `--check`              | `-c`  |         | Check formatting, do not modify files |
| `--print`              | `-p`  |         | Print to stdout, do not modify files |
| `--fail-on-change`     | `-f`  |         | Fail if files are modified |
| `--recursive`          | `-r`  |         | Recursively search for files to format |
| `--nowrap`             | `-n`  |         | Do not wrap long lines |
| `--wraplen <N>`        | `-l`  | `80`    | Line length for wrapping |
| `--tabsize <N>`        | `-t`  | `2`     | Number of characters to use as tab size |
| `--usetabs`            |       |         | Use tabs instead of spaces for indentation |
| `--stdin`              | `-s`  |         | Process stdin as a single file, output to stdout |
| `--config <PATH>`      |       |         | Path to config file |
| `--noconfig`           |       |         | Do not read any config file |
| `--verbose`            | `-v`  |         | Show info messages |
| `--quiet`              | `-q`  |         | Hide warning messages |
| `--trace`              |       |         | Show trace messages |
| `--completion <SHELL>` |       |         | Generate a shell completion script |
| `--man`                |       |         | Generate a man page |
| `--args`               |       |         | View arguments passed to tex-fmt |
| `--help`               | `-h`  |         | Print help |
| `--version`            | `-V`  |         | Print version |

### Configuration file options

The following arguments can be provided in `tex-fmt.toml`.
The first example in each row is the default value.

| Option           | Type     | Examples               | Description |
| ---------------- | -------- | ---------------------- | --- |
| `check`          | bool     | `false`                | Check formatting, do not modify files |
| `print`          | bool     | `false`                | Print to stdout, do not modify files |
| `fail-on-change` | bool     | `false`                | Fail if files are modified |
| `wrap`           | bool     | `true`                 | Wrap long lines |
| `wraplen`        | int      | `80`, `100`            | Line length for wrapping |
| `wrapmin`        | int      | `70`, `90`             | Target minimum length for line wrapping |
| `tabsize`        | int      | `2`, `4`               | Number of characters to use as tab size |
| `tabchar`        | str      | `"space"`, `"tab"`     | Character to use for indentation |
| `stdin`          | bool     | `false`                | Process stdin as a single file, output to stdout |
| `lists`          | arr[str] | `[]`, `["myitemize"]`  | Extra list environments to be formatted as `itemize` |
| `verbatims`      | arr[str] | `[]`, `["myverbatim"]` | Extra verbatim environments |
| `no-indent-envs` | arr[str] | `[]`, `["mydocument"]` | Environments which are not indented |
| `wrap-chars`     | arr[str] | `[]`, `["。"]`         | Characters after which lines may be wrapped |
| `verbosity`      | str      | `"warn"`, `"error"`    | Verbosity level for terminal logging |

"""Regression examples recorded while exercising the documented CLI."""
import importlib.util
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'src'))
from formatter import Formatter, FormattingError
from settings import parse_args, resolve, describe


def format_text(text, *args, updates=None):
    cli, _ = parse_args(['--noconfig', *args], 'executable')
    options = resolve(cli)
    if updates:
        options.update(updates)
    logs = []
    output = Formatter(options, lambda *message: logs.append(message)).format(text)
    return output, logs


class FormattingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_environment_and_list_indentation(self):
        text = ('\\begin{document}\n  hello\n\\begin{itemize}\n'
                '\\item First\ncontinued\n\\item Second\n'
                '\\end{itemize}\n\\begin{equation}\nx=2\n'
                '\\end{equation}\n\\end{document}')
        expected = ('\\begin{document}\nhello\n\\begin{itemize}\n'
                    '  \\item First\n    continued\n  \\item Second\n'
                    '\\end{itemize}\n\\begin{equation}\n  x=2\n'
                    '\\end{equation}\n\\end{document}\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], expected)

    def test_inline_environments_are_separated(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_text('a\\begin{e}b\\end{e}c')[0],
                         'a\n\\begin{e}b\n\\end{e}c\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('\\begin{a} \\begin{b}\nx\n\\end{b} \\end{a}')[0],
                         '\\begin{a}\n  \\begin{b}\n    x\n  \\end{b}\n\\end{a}\n')

    def test_braces_brackets_and_parentheses(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_text('\\foo{\nx\n{\ny\n}\n}\n')[0],
                         '\\foo{\n  x\n  {\n    y\n  }\n}\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('(\nx\n)\n\\[\nx\n\\]\n')[0],
                         '(\n  x\n)\n\\[\n  x\n\\]\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('{x\ny} z {q\nr}\n')[0],
                         '{x\ny} z {q\nr}\n')

    def test_conditionals_are_not_structural(self):
        text = '\\iftrue\nx\n\\else\ny\n\\fi\n$$\nx\n$$\n'
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], text)

    def test_comments_and_escaped_percent(self):
        text = '\\begin{a}\n% {\nx \\% {\ny\n}\n\\end{a}\n'
        expected = '\\begin{a}\n  % {\n  x \\% {\n    y\n  }\n\\end{a}\n'
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], expected)

    def test_verbatim_block(self):
        text = '\\begin{verbatim}\n   a\n    b  \n\\begin{foo}\n  \\end{verbatim}\nx\n'
        expected = '\\begin{verbatim}\n   a\n    b\n\\begin{foo}\n  \\end{verbatim}\nx\n'
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], expected)

    def test_formatter_directives(self):
        text = ('\\begin{a}\n   x % tex-fmt: skip\n'
                '   % tex-fmt: off\n x\n    y\n   % tex-fmt: on\n'
                'x\n\\end{a}\n')
        expected = ('\\begin{a}\n   x % tex-fmt: skip\n'
                    '   % tex-fmt: off\n x\n    y\n   % tex-fmt: on\n'
                    '  x\n\\end{a}\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], expected)
        # A trailing space on a final unterminated line is significant.
        self.assertEqual(format_text('   x % tex-fmt: skip ')[0],
                         'x % tex-fmt: skip\n')

    def test_blank_line_normalization(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_text('')[0], '\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('a\n\n\n\nb\n\n')[0], 'a\n\nb\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('a\n \n \n \nb\n')[0], 'a\n\n\n\nb\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('a\r\n\r\n\r\nb\r\n')[0], 'a\n\n\nb\n')

    def test_default_wrap_target(self):
        text = ' '.join('word'+str(i) for i in range(25))
        expected = ('word0 word1 word2 word3 word4 word5 word6 word7 word8 word9 word10\n'
                    'word11 word12 word13 word14 word15 word16 word17 word18 word19 word20\n'
                    'word21 word22 word23 word24\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text)[0], expected)
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text, '--nowrap')[0], text+'\n')

    def test_wrap_comment_prefix(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_text('%% abc def ghi jkl mno', '-l', '10')[0],
                         '%% abc\n% def ghi\n% jkl mno\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('text % abc def ghi jkl mno', '-l', '10')[0],
                         'text %\n% abc def\n% ghi jkl\n% mno\n')

    def test_wrapping_recalculates_indentation(self):
        text = '\\textbf{' + 'abc '*30 + '}'
        expected = ('\\textbf{abc abc abc abc abc\n'
                    '  abc abc abc abc abc abc abc\n'
                    '  abc abc abc abc abc abc abc\n'
                    '  abc abc abc abc abc abc abc\n'
                    'abc abc abc abc }\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text, '-l', '30')[0], expected)

    def test_inline_verbatim_wrap_protection(self):
        text = '\\verb|one two three four five six| after rest'
        expected = '\\verb|one two three four five six|\nafter rest\n'
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text, '-l', '20')[0], expected)
        with self.assertRaises(FormattingError):
            format_text('\\verb|one two three four five', '-l', '20')

    def test_unicode_wrapping(self):
        self.assertEqual(format_text('你好你好 你好你好 你好你好', '-l', '10')[0],
                         '你好你好 你好你好\n你好你好\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('aaa,bbb,ccc,ddd,eee', '-l', '10',
                                    updates={'wrap-chars':[',',' ']})[0],
                         'aaa,bbb,\nccc,ddd,\neee\n')

    def test_tab_indentation(self):
        text = '\\begin{a}\n x\n  y\n\\end{a}\n'
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text, '--usetabs')[0],
                         '\\begin{a}\n\t\tx\n  y\n\\end{a}\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text('a\tb\n')[0], 'a  b\n')
        self.assertEqual(format_text(text, '-t', '0')[0],
                         '\\begin{a}\nx\ny\n\\end{a}\n')

    def test_negative_indentation_diagnostics(self):
        output, logs = format_text('}\nx\n')
        self.assertEqual(output, '}\nx\n')
        warnings = [m[1] for m in logs if m[0]=='warn']
        self.assertEqual(warnings, [
            'Line 1 (1). Indent is negative.',
            'Line 2 (2). Indent is negative.',
            'Indent does not return to zero. Last non-indented line is line 1',
            'Negative indents. First negatively indented line is line 1'])

    def test_argument_dump(self):
        options = resolve(parse_args(['--noconfig','-s','-t','4','-l','30'], 'executable')[0])
        text = describe(options, [])
        self.assertIn('  tabsize:                 4\n', text)
        self.assertIn('  wrapmin:                 30\n', text)
        self.assertIn('  fail-on-change:          true\n', text)


class CommandLineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.executable = ROOT/'build'/'test-executable'
        subprocess.run([str(ROOT/'compile.sh'), str(cls.executable)], check=True)

    def run_cli(self, args, data='', cwd=None, config=True):
        cmd = [str(self.executable)] + (['--noconfig'] if config else []) + list(args)
        return subprocess.run(cmd, input=data, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=cwd)

    def test_stdin_and_version(self):
        p = self.run_cli(['-s'], '  abc\n')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr), (0,'abc\n',''))
        p = self.run_cli(['--version'])
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'tex-fmt 0.5.6\n')

    def test_check_print_and_write(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            path = Path(tmp)/'a.tex'
            path.write_text('  abc\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-c',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertEqual(path.read_text(), '  abc\n')
            self.assertEqual(p.stderr, f'ERROR: tex-fmt {path}: Incorrect formatting. \n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-c','-p',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout), (0,'abc\n'))
            p = self.run_cli(['-f',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertEqual(path.read_text(), 'abc\n')
            self.assertEqual(self.run_cli(['-f',str(path)]).returncode, 0)

    def test_config_and_cli_overrides(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            (Path(tmp)/'tex-fmt.toml').write_text('tabsize=4\nwrap=false\nlists=["foo"]\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-s','-t','1'], '\\begin{foo}\n\\item x\ny\n\\end{foo}\n',
                             cwd=tmp, config=False)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, '\\begin{foo}\n \\item x\n  y\n\\end{foo}\n')

    def test_recursive_ignores_and_extensions(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root/'.git').mkdir()
            (root/'a.tex').write_text(' a\n')
            (root/'b.tex').write_text(' b\n')
            (root/'c.txt').write_text(' c\n')
            (root/'.hidden.tex').write_text(' hidden\n')
            (root/'.gitignore').write_text('b.tex\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-r','-p'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr), (0,'a\n',''))
            p = self.run_cli(['-r','-p','a'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'a\n')

    def test_adjacent_duplicate_paths(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root/'a.tex').write_text(' a\n')
            (root/'b.tex').write_text(' b\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-p','a','a.tex','b.tex','a.tex'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'a\nb\na\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

cat > IMPLEMENTATION.md <<'EOF'
# Independent implementation

This code implements the documented command-line interface using only Python's
standard library. Its behavior was established by running the supplied program
with small examples, diagnostic flags, configuration files, and temporary file
trees. No original implementation or project dependencies are used.

## Build and test

```sh
./compile.sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The build creates a self-contained executable Python archive at `./executable`.
Python 3.10 or newer is the only prerequisite and no packages need downloading.
An optional output filename can be supplied to `compile.sh` for development.
All build outputs and local observation files are ignored by Git.

## Organization

- `src/formatter.py`: line normalization, indentation, environment separation,
  wrapping, formatter directives, and diagnostic events.
- `src/settings.py`: argument parsing, TOML configuration, defaults, and argument
  display.
- `src/__main__.py`: file discovery, ignore rules, I/O modes, and terminal output.
- `src/assets/`: static CLI documentation and completion output templates.
- `tests/test_formatter.py`: formatting and command-line regression tests.

Formatting uses a queue of lines. When a line is divided, its fragments retain
its original line number. A fragment is re-evaluated before output, since a
split can separate an opening delimiter from its closing delimiter. Actual and
visual indentation are maintained separately. Configuration and I/O behavior
are likewise tested separately from the formatting engine.

class CommandLineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.executable = ROOT/'build'/'test-executable'
        subprocess.run([str(ROOT/'compile.sh'), str(cls.executable)], check=True)

    def run_cli(self, args, data='', cwd=None, config=True):
        cmd = [str(self.executable)] + (['--noconfig'] if config else []) + list(args)
        return subprocess.run(cmd, input=data, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=cwd)

    def test_stdin_and_version(self):
        p = self.run_cli(['-s'], '  abc\n')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr), (0,'abc\n',''))
        p = self.run_cli(['--version'])
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'tex-fmt 0.5.6\n')

    def test_check_print_and_write(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            path = Path(tmp)/'a.tex'
            path.write_text('  abc\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-c',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertEqual(path.read_text(), '  abc\n')
            self.assertEqual(p.stderr, f'ERROR: tex-fmt {path}: Incorrect formatting. \n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-c','-p',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout), (0,'abc\n'))
            p = self.run_cli(['-f',str(path)])
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertEqual(path.read_text(), 'abc\n')
            self.assertEqual(self.run_cli(['-f',str(path)]).returncode, 0)

    def test_config_and_cli_overrides(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            (Path(tmp)/'tex-fmt.toml').write_text('tabsize=4\nwrap=false\nlists=["foo"]\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-s','-t','1'], '\\begin{foo}\n\\item x\ny\n\\end{foo}\n',
                             cwd=tmp, config=False)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, '\\begin{foo}\n \\item x\n  y\n\\end{foo}\n')

    def test_recursive_ignores_and_extensions(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root/'.git').mkdir()
            (root/'a.tex').write_text(' a\n')
            (root/'b.tex').write_text(' b\n')
            (root/'c.txt').write_text(' c\n')
            (root/'.hidden.tex').write_text(' hidden\n')
            (root/'.gitignore').write_text('b.tex\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-r','-p'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr), (0,'a\n',''))
            p = self.run_cli(['-r','-p','a'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'a\n')

    def test_adjacent_duplicate_paths(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root/'a.tex').write_text(' a\n')
            (root/'b.tex').write_text(' b\n')
            p = self.run_cli(['-p','a','a.tex','b.tex','a.tex'], cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'a\nb\na\n')

# Independent implementation

This code implements the documented command-line interface using only Python's
standard library. Its behavior was established by running the supplied program
with small examples, diagnostic flags, configuration files, and temporary file
trees. No original implementation or project dependencies are used.

## Build and test

```sh

```

The build creates a self-contained executable Python archive at `./executable`.
Python 3.10 or newer is the only prerequisite and no packages need downloading.
An optional output filename can be supplied to `compile.sh` for development.
All build outputs and local observation files are ignored by Git.

## Organization

- `src/formatter.py`: line normalization, indentation, environment separation,
  wrapping, formatter directives, and diagnostic events.
- `src/settings.py`: argument parsing, TOML configuration, defaults, and argument
  display.
- `src/__main__.py`: file discovery, ignore rules, I/O modes, and terminal output.
- `src/assets/`: static CLI documentation and completion output templates.
- `tests/test_formatter.py`: formatting and command-line regression tests.

Formatting uses a queue of lines. When a line is divided, its fragments retain
its original line number. A fragment is re-evaluated before output, since a
split can separate an opening delimiter from its closing delimiter. Actual and
visual indentation are maintained separately. Configuration and I/O behavior
are likewise tested separately from the formatting engine.
